headline: Every part of reference 02/03 is present, correctly placed and correctly lit — the material now measures within a few points of the art on every axis — and the only thing a person would call out side by side is the electricity itself, which is drawn as untapered polylines with free-ending branches instead of the reference's tapering filaments; that fix lives in src/fx, not on this screen.

findings.what: The arcs are constant-width, round-capped polylines with branches that stop dead in mid-air, where the reference's filaments taper to nothing and kink at several times the frequency. Visible at REST, not only on commit.
findings.evidence: In /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ilyakarakotov-Documents-GitHub-junkyard-camp/88d17ba8-b7d4-43ff-8bdc-47453cc9aca8/scratchpad/shots/signoff-rollcall.png, the idle filament inside the glass tube throws a branch that leaves the main path at ~x=430 and ends at device (467,1436) — full stroke width, blunt end, ~13px short of the right electrode's face (x=479) and ~40px below the bore axis. Cropped at 8x it is unmistakably a line that terminates on nothing, which CLAUDE.md calls non-negotiable. The main filament shows ~7 direction changes across the 180-device-px bore; the reference's (02, x=400-700) wanders continuously with roughly three times that density and a visibly larger excursion. Same generator on commit (shots/signoff-commit.png, driven by selecting RUST CO. then Enter on role=slider): each bolt is a uniform-width band whose tips end bluntly on the plate — the fork at ~(190,1275) and the lower branches near (215,1420) — while 03's bolts taper to hairlines at every tip. The broad even bloom that results is also why commit measures medL 90 / spec 3.58 against the reference's 83 / 4.4: bloom area is spread rather than concentrated in a tight core.
findings.fix: In src/fx/arcPaths.ts raise buildBolt's kink frequency to 3-4x the displacement amplitude (currently segments≈len/9 against amp≈len*0.09, i.e. one segment per unit of displacement), and taper branch strokeWidth to 0 at the free end. In src/fx/Arc.tsx drop strokeLinecap='round' on the branch layer and keep the two-layer order (thin white-hot core over thicker teal glow) on branches, not just on the trunk — the tube's tail branch currently has no white core at all. A tapered bolt sheds bloom area on its own, which should also close the commit-state brightness gap.

findings.what: The lever grip has no focus or selection styling, so pulling it introduces the one thing CLAUDE.md forbids outright: cool blue-grey.

findings.what: The team seal's circular legend is roughly 40% of the reference's cap height and set with runaway tracking, so it reads as a ring of spaced ticks rather than a struck name.
findings.evidence: src/components/TeamCrest.tsx sets fontSize={label.length > 15 ? 4 : 4.6} on a 64-unit viewBox, so "RUST REVIVAL CO." (16 chars) renders at 4 units — cap height ~2.9/64 = 4.5% of the coin diameter. Measured on the reference (design/reference/v2/05-team-sheet.jpg) the legend's cap height is ~40 image px on a 415px coin = 9.6%. Compounding it, textPath carries textLength={Math.min(86, ...)} with lengthAdjust="spacing", which stretches a short name across 200deg of arc; in my crop (scratchpad/shots/b-coin.png vs r-coin.png) the reference's letters touch each other while ours are separated by more than a letter width, and the trailing "C.O." runs into the coin's edge shadow. The reference's legend is the second most legible thing on the screen after the total; ours reads as texture.
findings.fix: In TeamCrest.tsx raise the seal's fontSize to about 8 (cap height ~9.5% of the 64 box), raise fontWeight to 700, and drop lengthAdjust="spacing" in favour of a textLength that scales with the name so tracking stays near-normal (or clamp the stretch to ~10% of the natural advance width). Only the `label` (seal) branch needs to change — the medallion variant has no legend.

findings.what: The RUST CO. emblem renders as a water droplet inside a gear, not the reference's flame with a wrench through it — and the droplet duplicates the CLEANLINESS category glyph (gear + droplet) sitting two rows below it on the same screen.
findings.evidence: EMBLEMS.rustco in src/components/TeamCrest.tsx builds the centrepiece as `M24 13.5 C26.6 18.2 29.2 20.4 29.2 24.6 A5.2 5.2 0 1 1 18.8 24.6 C18.8 20.4 21.4 18.2 24 13.5 Z` — two curves converging to a point over a 5.2r circle, which is the canonical teardrop, plus `M20.4 30.4 L27.6 30.4 ... Z`, a 7.2x3.7 rectangle with two notches that reads as a chip at render size. The comment above it claims "a gear ring behind a flame, with a wrench jaw beneath"; the render does not show that. Side by side at 2.4x (scratchpad/shots/b-coin.png vs r-coin.png) the reference's centrepiece is an asymmetric multi-tongued flame with a wrench shaft running from the bore down to a round bolt end, filling ~70% of the coin; ours is a symmetric teardrop with a small square under it. The Breaker CLEANLINESS glyph one row down is also gear + droplet, so the team's identity mark and a category icon are near-identical drawings on one screen.
findings.fix: Redraw EMBLEMS.rustco: give the flame two or three asymmetric tongues (unequal heights, one licking left) instead of a symmetric teardrop, and replace the notched rectangle with a real wrench — an open jaw at the top, a shaft down the emblem's vertical axis, and a round bolt terminal at the bottom, as in the reference. Keep the evenodd non-overlap discipline the current path already respects. Verify the silhouette is distinguishable from the CLEANLINESS droplet at 26px on a board row.

findings.what: The header's brass band is a flat near-white strip carrying a stray dark hairline, where the reference's is a shaded gold casting with a single monotonic falloff.
findings.evidence: Column scan down the band clear of the coin, x=140 in my screenshot: L175, 174, 178, **109**, 180, then 41 (the engraved groove) — a bright/dark/bright sandwich inside an otherwise flat field that never varies more than 4 luma across its 8 CSS width. The same scan on the reference at x=180: L169, 135, 122, 126, 47 — a continuous fall of 47 luma with no spike. REFERENCE-SPEC hardware item 3 asks for "outer bevel ... lit top-left, --brass-lo bottom-right"; at this flatness the band has no bevel gradient to read. At 4.5x (scratchpad/shots/b-corner.png vs r-corner.png) the corner also shows the engraved inner line breaking into two disconnected segments that stop short of the fillet, so the horizontal and vertical bands read as two overlapping strips rather than one machined part.
findings.fix: In src/components/chrome.tsx `.brass-band`, remove the hard-capped near-white sheen stop (the same one already stripped from `.plate` and the crest bezel) and let the band run --brass-hi at the top to --brass-lo at the bottom-right. Separately give BrassFrame a `lineRadius` prop (or derive it from the child's radius) so the engraved line follows the 12px opening fillet instead of `Math.max(1, radius - 2)` off the outer radius.
